We need a retrosynthesis route with max 1 step (i.e., a single reaction) from commercially available precursors, total price <= $250. The target SMILES is a complex molecule: an alkene attached to phenyl, plus a cyclobutane? Actually structure: [CH2]=[C] attached to phenyl and a chiral cyclobutane with OH and CF3. The template 1229769 gave precursors: C=C(c1ccccc1)[C@@H]1CCCC1=O (a cyclopentanone? Actually C=C(c1ccccc1) attached to a cyclobutanone? Wait SMILES: C=C(c1ccccc1)[C@@H]1CCCC1=O is an alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone with phenyl and cyclobutanone? It's a cyclobutanone? Actually [C@@H]1CCCC1=O is cyclobutanone? No, 5-membered? C1CCCC1=O is cyclopentanone. So product is an unsaturated ketone. The other precursor is C[Si](C)(C)C(F)(F)F (a trifluoromethylsilane). The template likely does a nucleophilic addition of CF3 to carbonyl? But verification failed. Maybe need different template.

We need a single-step synthesis: maybe use a known reaction: addition of CF3- to a carbonyl to give CF3-substituted alcohol? Our target has CF3 attached to carbon bearing OH and cyclobutane. Actually target: C@ (CF3)(OH) attached to cyclobutane. So could be formed by addition of CF3- to a ketone (the cyclobutanone) to give tertiary alcohol with CF3. The other part is the alkene phenyl attached to same carbon? Wait target: [CH2]=[C]([c1ccccc1])C@@H1CCCC1(OH)C(F)(F)F. So the carbon bearing OH and CF3 is attached to cyclobutane and also to the alkene carbon (sp2). So it's a tertiary carbon with CF3, OH, and attached to cyclobutane and alkene phenyl. That suggests starting from the unsaturated ketone C=C(c1ccccc1)C(=O)cyclobutane? Actually the carbonyl would be at that carbon, then addition of CF3- gives CF3 and OH. So precursor could be the ketone: C=C(c1ccccc1)C(=O)C1CCCC1 (i.e., alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone). That is C=C(c1ccccc1)C(=O)C1CCCC1. Let's see if that is commercially available. Search.
